groups.canonical_name: Commodity and semiconductor input cost inflation
groups.definition: Rising costs of metals, semiconductors and other inputs raise production costs that may not be passed on to customers.
Semiconductor industry cyclicality, overcapacity and customer order fluctuations cause volatile revenue, price erosion and under-utilization.

groups.canonical_name: Dependence on subcontracted wafer fabrication suppliers
groups.definition: Reliance on subcontractors for wafer fabrication, assembly and test with few alternates risks supply disruption.

groups.canonical_name: Semiconductor wafer and materials supply shortage
groups.definition: Limited-source suppliers of wafers, materials and equipment may fail to provide sufficient supply, constraining production and raising costs.
Losing a design-in during long automotive design cycles can block access to customers for years.

groups.canonical_name: Vehicle emissions and fuel economy regulation
groups.definition: Evolving and divergent emissions, fuel economy and EV regulations impose compliance costs, credit purchases, penalties and limits on profitable vehicle sales.

groups.canonical_name: EV adoption and battery supply limits
groups.definition: Slow EV infrastructure, consumer acceptance and battery raw material supply constrain profitable EV growth and compliance.

groups.canonical_name: New vehicle launch and acceptance risk
groups.definition: Long, costly vehicle development cycles risk launches that fail to gain market acceptance, leaving high fixed costs.

groups.canonical_name: Profit concentration in full-size ICE trucks
groups.definition: Heavy reliance on high-margin full-size ICE trucks and SUVs exposes profits to oil price spikes and fuel economy rules.

groups.canonical_name: Technological obsolescence and semiconductor price erosion
groups.definition: Rapid technological change and competition shorten product life cycles and erode prices, requiring heavy R&D with uncertain returns.
Costs of supplier component defects found years later may not be recoverable due to supplier financial condition.
Just-in-time production with single-source parts makes vehicle output vulnerable to supplier disruptions.

groups.canonical_name: Technology disruption from new automotive competitors
groups.definition: New entrants in EVs, autonomous driving and mobility services threaten the core business if the company fails to commercialize new technologies.

groups.canonical_name: Working capital volatility from long product cycles
groups.definition: Long development-to-delivery periods drive high inventory and work-in-progress, causing working capital volatility.
